title: MHC-II deficiency in a large Algerian cohort: Clinical, immunological, and genetic characterization.
authors: Lamara Mahammed L, Belaid B, Chan KW, Mohand-Oussaid A, Drali O, Dehimi A, Leung D, Berkani LM
abstract: MHC class II (MHC-II) deficiency is a rare inborn error of immunity caused by defects in transcriptional regulators of MHC-II expression. In this study, we characterized the clinical, immunological, and molecular features of 107 patients from 98 unrelated Algerian families. Median ages at symptom onset and diagnosis were 5 and 14 mo, respectively, with pneumonia (82%) and chronic diarrhea (73%) predominating. CD4+ T cell lymphopenia occurred in 87.6% and naïve CD4+ T cell depletion in 86.0%. Among 99 genetically characterized patients, variants were identified exclusively in RFXANK (77.8%) and RFXAP (22.2%), including two predominant mutations (RFXANK c.338-25_338del and RFXAP c.368del) and four novel variants. Exploratory comparisons suggested a more severe phenotype in patients carrying RFXAP c.368del than in those carrying RFXANK c.338-25_338del. Five of seven transplanted patients survived versus 33.3% of non-transplanted patients. As the largest MHC-II deficiency cohort reported to date, this study substantially expands current knowledge of the disease and supports targeted genetic diagnosis in North African populations.

title: Comorbid asthma - occurrence and associations with patient-related outcomes in COPD: a cohort study.
authors: Athlin Å, Lisspers K, Hasselgren M, Ställberg B, Sandelowsky H, Giezeman M, Janson C, Kisiel MA
journal: Scandinavian journal of primary health care
abstract: PURPOSE: Clinical features of COPD and asthma overlap, complicating differential diagnosis. This study investigated the prevalence of comorbid asthma in COPD patients and its association with patient-related outcomes. MATERIALS AND METHODS: Patients with a doctor's diagnosis of COPD were randomly selected in two cohorts 2005 (n = 1060) and 2014 (n = 1671), from primary and secondary care in Sweden. Data were collected from medical records and patient questionnaires at baseline and at follow-up (2012 and 2022, respectively). Questionnaires included data on exacerbations. Symptoms were assessed using the clinical COPD questionnaire (CCQ). Comorbid asthma was identified through medical records. Ten-year mortality data were obtained from national registers. Logistic and linear regression assessed associations with patient-reported outcomes; Cox regression was applied for mortality analyses. RESULTS: Comorbid asthma was found in 22% of the 2005 cohort and 9% of the 2014 cohort (p < .001). In both cohorts, it was associated with an increased risk of exacerbations: OR (95% CI) 1.58 (1.07-2.32), p = .02, and 2.20 (1.38-3.52), p < .001, respectively. No associations were found between comorbid asthma and worsening of health status (CCQ). Mortality risk did not differ in the 2005 cohort, HR (95% CI) 0.92 (0.71-1.18), but was lower in the 2014 cohort, HR (95% CI) 0.67 (0.49-0.93), p = .02. CONCLUSION: Comorbid asthma in COPD has changed from 22 to 9%, potentially due to improved diagnostics. Comorbid asthma remains clinically relevant due to its association with an increased exacerbation risk.

title: Acute Kidney Disease and Clinical Outcomes in Stable Outpatients With Decompensated Cirrhosis: A Prospective Cohort Study.
authors: Lekakis V, Wong F, Papatheodoridis G, Vlachogiannakos J, Cholongitas E
journal: Journal of clinical and experimental hepatology
abstract: BACKGROUND/AIMS: Acute kidney disease (AKD), as recently redefined by the Acute Disease Quality Initiative-International Club of Ascites (ADQI-ICA) consensus, captures persistent or subacute kidney dysfunction often following acute kidney injury (AKI). Its prognostic relevance in stable outpatients with decompensated cirrhosis remains insufficiently characterized. This study aimed to evaluate the associations of AKD and its phenotypes (AKI-AKD and non-AKI AKD [NAKI-AKD]) with cirrhosis-related complications and mortality in outpatients with stable decompensated cirrhosis. METHODS: In this prospective real-world study, 131 patients were followed for up to 60 mo. AKD was defined according to ADQI-ICA criteria and modeled as a time-dependent exposure. Complications were analyzed using Poisson incidence rate and cause-specific Cox models. Mortality was assessed using Aalen-Johansen estimates and time-dependent cause-specific Cox regression, with liver transplantation considered a competing event and parsimonious adjustment for baseline liver disease severity. RESULTS: AKD developed in 51 patients (38.9%). The overall complication-event rate was higher following AKD onset than during AKD-free follow-up (183.3 vs 36.6 per 100 person-years; adjusted incidence rate ratio: 4.91, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 3.01-8.03; P < 0.001). In the MELD 3.0-adjusted model, the mortality hazard was highest during the AKD period (0-90 d after onset [adjusted cause-specific hazard ratio (aCsHR): 27.07, 95% CI: 11.83-61.90; P < 0.001]) and remained elevated during the late follow-up after AKD (aCsHR: 8.77, 95% CI: 4.00-19.23; P < 0.001). Among patients with AKD, AKI-AKD was associated with higher mortality than NAKI-AKD (aCsHR: 3.07, 95% CI: 1.46-6.47; P = 0.003). CONCLUSION: AKD is common among stable outpatients with decompensated cirrhosis and was associated with a graded risk of complications and death. Phenotypic stratification identifies AKI-AKD as the highest-risk subgroup, although these findings require confirmation in larger prospective studies.

title: Aptamer-CRISPR/Cas as a tool in point-of-care testing of infectious diseases.
authors: Lau CH, Huang Y, Ch'ng ES, Tang TH, Zhu H, Citartan M
abstract: Aptamers and the CRISPR/Cas system have become the cornerstones of target detections due to their numerous advantages. Aptamers enable direct recognition of non-nucleic acid targets, such as pathogens and antigens, while CRISPR/Cas system drives signal amplification and rapid detection. The combined aptamer-CRISPR/Cas system can overcome the limitations of traditional target detection by realizing field-deployable, highly sensitive, specific, versatile, and rapid assays. Given the increasing number of different aptamer-CRISPR/Cas systems developed recently, particularly for infectious diseases, we provide a comprehensive overview of these platforms designed for detecting significant viruses such as SARS-CoV-2, Monkeypox virus, Hepatitis B virus and bacteria that include Mycobacterium tuberculosis, Staphylococcus aureus and Salmonella. Current challenges that impede the deployment of aptamer-CRISPR/Cas for point-of-care pathogen detection were also mapped, including primary barriers such as clinical matrix effect and stability. Several strategies to mitigate these issues were also set forth, predominantly the integration of artificial intelligence and machine learning to accelerate the transition of aptamer-CRISPR/Cas system to the clinical translation and commercialization phase, paving the way towards widespread implementation in global health.

title: Transposable elements as dual agents in livestock-parasite interactions: From parasite adaptation to host genetic innovation.
authors: Omara A, Moawad AS, Ge J, Geng T
abstract: Transposable elements (TEs), which were previously seen as genomic parasites, are currently viewed as major contributors to evolutionary innovation in host-parasite interactions. This review provides an overview of the current knowledge of TEs in veterinary parasitology, divided into three interlinked levels. Firstly, in terms of parasite genome biology, TEs are highly diverse and actively transposing, from the extremely active mobilomes of strongylid nematodes and liver flukes to the TE-rich but genomically reduced microsporidian parasites. Secondly, at the host-parasite interface, direct physical contacts help in the horizontal exchange of TEs between the parasites and their hosts. Thirdly, TE activity leads to important functional innovations, including expansions of virulence-related gene families in schistosomes, formation of species-specific stage-regulated non-coding RNAs in liver flukes, and even TE-derived small interfering RNAs secreted by parasitic nematodes as cross-species immune modulators. On the host side, polymorphic TEs, especially SINEs and endogenous retroviruses, provide abundant opportunities to generate phenotypic diversity in livestock by affecting features such as muscle formation, fat accumulation, fur coloration, and immune response. Throughout this review, we clearly separate the established facts from the associations and hypotheses, and highlight the areas of knowledge deficit. In conclusion, we will outline the model of utilizing TE biomarkers in selective breeding, and note that the association between particular polymorphisms of TEs and resistance to parasites is mostly hypothetical and needs further verification.

title: When the earth shakes on fragile foundations: the Venezuelan earthquakes and two decades of public health system erosion.
authors: Paníz-Mondolfi AE, Chaccour C, Carrión-Nessi FS, Acosta-Serrano Á, Zambrano O, Gabaldón-Figueira JC, Grillet ME
abstract: The two earthquakes that recently struck the northern coast of Venezuela will deepen a health crisis that has troubled the country for twenty years. They have exposed how weak its health infrastructure is, how scarce medicines are, how little epidemiological surveillance remains, and how long investment has been lacking. The humanitarian health crisis in Venezuela did not arise from armed conflict, as it has elsewhere. Its roots lie in decades of authoritarian rule and institutional decay, which have eroded public health capacity, research infrastructure, vaccination coverage and the control of infectious diseases in general. Because these weaknesses have accumulated, the earthquakes may well turn into an even graver humanitarian emergency. Recovery that lasts will not be secured by short-term international aid alone. It will require the rebuilding of accountable institutions able to govern transparently and to apply equitable health policies, so that the health system can regain its resilience.

title: Magnoflorine alleviates depression-like behaviors via modulation of serotonergic signaling and neurotrophic pathways.
authors: Zhao Y, Gong Y, Li H, Ren L, Zhao X, Chen Z
abstract: Depression is a prevalent and debilitating psychiatric disorder characterized by dysregulation of monoaminergic neurotransmission and impaired neuroplasticity, and current antidepressants are limited by delayed onset and suboptimal efficacy, necessitating novel multi-target therapeutics. Magnoflorine, an alkaloid derived from Ziziphi Spinosae Semen (Suanzaoren), has been reported to possess antianxiety and neuroprotective activities, but its antidepressant effects and underlying mechanisms remain unclear. This study employed an integrated strategy combining network pharmacology, molecular docking, molecular dynamics simulation, and experimental validation to investigate the antidepressant effects of magnoflorine. The effects of magnoflorine were evaluated in corticosterone (CORT)-induced HT-22 cells and a chronic unpredictable mild stress (CUMS) mouse model using behavioral tests, neurochemical analysis, histological analysis, and Western blotting. Network pharmacology analysis suggested that magnoflorine may regulate multiple targets involved in depression, particularly serotonergic signaling pathways. Molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulations suggested potential interactions between magnoflorine and 5-HT1AR/SERT. In vitro and in vivo experiments demonstrated that magnoflorine ameliorated CORT-induced neuronal injury and CUMS-associated depression-like behaviors, restored hippocampal monoamine levels, and alleviated neuronal damage. These effects were accompanied by alterations in 5-HT1AR and SERT expression and enhanced ERK phosphorylation and BDNF expression. Collectively, these findings suggest that the antidepressant-like effects of magnoflorine are associated with modulation of serotonergic and neurotrophic signaling.

title: Identification of neoechinulin B metabolites in vivo by UPLC Q/TOF MS and exploration of its anti HCV mechanism based on network pharmacology and molecular docking.
authors: Ren X, Lu XH, Chen YF, Tu XP, Li BY, Tao X, Yang X, Zhang FX
journal: Journal of pharmaceutical and biomedical analysis
abstract: Fungal secondary metabolites, owing to their structural diversity and broad spectrum of bioactivities, have become a vital source for the discovery of microbial drugs and antiviral lead compounds. Fungi of the genus Aspergillus, which are ubiquitous filamentous microorganisms, are capable of producing structurally novel and functionally diverse secondary metabolites, thus representing a rich reservoir for drug lead discovery. Neoechinulin B (NeoB), an isoprenyl indole diketopiperazine alkaloid isolated from Aspergillus strains, exhibits potent antiviral activity. However, its poor characterization in terms of in vivo metabolism has hindered further development. In this work, we systematically explored the metabolic profile of NeoB in Sprague-Dawley rats, and combined network pharmacology with molecular docking to generate hypotheses regarding its potential anti‑HCV mechanism. These computational results are predictive and require future experimental validation. Following oral administration of NeoB to rats at 20 mg/kg/day, a total of 18 compounds, including NeoB and its metabolites, were identified in plasma, urine, faeces, heart, and liver. The proposed major metabolic pathways involved demethylation, sulfation, and glucuronidation. Network pharmacology and molecular docking were then used to generate hypotheses regarding potential anti-HCV targets. These computational results are predictive and require future experimental validation. Network pharmacology suggested that NeoB and its representative metabolites may potentially modulate targets such as SRC and EGFR, and by interfering with signalling pathways including "Proteoglycans in cancer" and "Hepatitis C". Molecular docking results suggested a potential preference for SRC over EGFR based on docking scores. However, because redocking validation for EGFR and SRC did not meets the 2.0 Å threshold, theses docking scores are considered computational estimates only. They cannot be used to infer target selectivity or differences in binding affinity. The parent compound P0 showed lowest docking score with SRC (-10.5 kcal/mol)), but this value is a computational estimate and does not represent experimental binding affinity. Overall, the docking outcomes were consistent with the network pharmacology predictions. This study qualitatively characterizes the in vivo metabolic profile of NeoB and provides computational hypotheses for future research. Any therapeutic implications remain speculative.

title: Tissue engineering polymeric formulations enable lymphangiogenesis for myocardial repair.
authors: Liu Z, Li R, Huang W, Zhang J, Qu Y, Dong W, Liu Y, Li Q
abstract: PURPOSE: Emerging evidence emphasizes the pivotal contribution of cardiac lymphatic activation following ischemic heart injury, with induced lymphangiogenesis driving edema resolution and inflammatory cell clearance. The aim of this study was to identify a bioactive small molecule with pro-lymphangiogenic activity and to develop a tissue engineering polymeric formulation for sustained local delivery in myocardial repair. METHODS: Through a high-throughput screen, we identified the bioactive molecule β-(3,4-dihydroxyphenyl) lactic acid (3,4-DHPLA) as a potent stimulator of lymphatic endothelial cells (LECs). To leverage this finding, we engineered a tissue engineering polymeric formulation (TEPF) to promote lymphangiogenesis during myocardial repair. The TEPF was fabricated via an integrated strategy combining 3D printing and near-field electrospinning to incorporate 3,4-DHPLA into a biodegradable polyurethane scaffold. The resulting structure mimics the microstructure of the cardiac extracellular matrix while supporting the microenvironment-responsive release of 3,4-DHPLA. RESULTS: We evaluated the therapeutic efficacy of TEPF in rat and porcine ischemia/reperfusion injury models, which markedly improved cardiac function and significantly attenuated adverse ventricular remodeling. Single-cell RNA sequencing and in vitro data further revealed the dual mechanisms of TEPF, not only promoting lymphangiogenesis but also orchestrating a pro-regenerative niche via expansion of Tregs, M2 macrophages, and pro-regenerative fibroblasts (COL12A1+, COL11A1+, NRG1+). CONCLUSIONS: Thus, the tissue engineering polymeric formulations may enable sustained drug release during myocardial tissue repair, thereby alleviating the pain of injection administration for patients with cardiovascular diseases and potentially facilitating patient-friendly use of other functional molecules-based therapeutic tissue engineering formulations through durable delivery.

title: Online chiral derivatization coupled with CE-MS for baseline separation of 16 proteinogenic amino acid enantiomers.
authors: Lu J, Gao W, Huang Q, Du L, Li H, Hu X, Wang C, Zhao Y
abstract: Amino acid (AA) enantiomers influence protein function through their distinct spatial structures, making their precise separation essential for elucidating physiological and pathological pathways. In this work, a novel method for the efficient separation of AA enantiomers based on on-line chiral derivatization with (S)-N-(4-nitrophenoxycarbonyl) phenylalanine methoxyethyl ester ((S)-NIFE) coupled with CE-MS has been developed. The method utilizes the ultrafast reaction kinetics of (S)-NIFE with AA enantiomers to facilitate their efficient separation. The online strategy eliminates time-consuming offline derivatization by permitting immediate injection upon simple mixing of derivatization reagent with AA enantiomers, enabling a streamlined analytical workflow. By optimizing experimental parameters, baseline separation of 16 chiral proteinogenic AA enantiomers has been achieved with resolutions ranging from 1.5 to 11.03. The relative standard deviations of migration time and peak area for intraday and interday measurements are less than 5%, and the limits of detection (LOD) and quantification (LOQ) are as low as 40 nM and 80 nM, respectively. Furthermore, the method was further applied to comparative analyses of AA enantiomers in serum samples from healthy controls and patients with non-alcoholic fatty liver disease and atrial fibrillation. The baseline separation of three AA enantiomers was consistently achieved. The LODs and LOQs for three ᴅ-AAs in complex matrix were as low as 180 nM and 600 nM. The intraday and interday precisions were both below 11%, and the average recoveries range from 87.60% to 95.51% with low standard deviations. All these results confirm the effectiveness of the approach in separating AA enantiomers in complex matrices.

title: A modular in vitro multienzyme cascade for the sustainable synthesis of high-value vidarabine 5'-monophosphate from adenosine.
authors: Su W, Zhang X, Li R, Li K, Guo X, Liu X, Wang Z, Wang H
abstract: Nucleoside analogues such as vidarabine (Ara-A) are vital therapeutics but are often limited by poor pharmacokinetics. Its phosphorylated form, vidarabine 5'-monophosphate (Ara-AMP), offers improved solubility and is used as a clinical alternative, although it can be dephosphorylated to Ara-A in vivo. Here, we report a modular multienzyme cascade for the sustainable synthesis of Ara-AMP directly from adenosine. The cascade integrates three functional modules: a core module (PNP, PPM, and RpiA) for the conversion of adenosine to Ara-A, a driver module (dNKδ20) for the selective phosphorylation of Ara-A to Ara-AMP, and a support module (PPK) for ATP regeneration from low-cost ADP and polyphosphate. The use of dNKδ20, a mutant deoxyribonucleoside kinase with high selectivity for Ara-A over adenosine, is critical for minimizing the formation of AMP byproduct, which would otherwise complicate downstream processing. Under optimized conditions, the cascade achieved an 80.2% conversion of 1 mM adenosine to Ara-AMP in 4 h using 0.05 mM ADP. The modular design was also applicable to guanosine and inosine, affording the corresponding arabinosyl nucleotides, albeit with lower yields. This work establishes a sustainable biocatalytic platform for nucleoside analogues, exemplifying how enzyme promiscuity, thermodynamic driving, and cofactor recycling enable green pharmaceutical manufacturing.

title: Reprogramming NOX4-associated ferro-aging with an iron-chelating senescent-cell-targeted therapy for intervertebral disc degeneration.
authors: Wang J, Chen Q, Xing J, Sun Y, Yan C, Zhao B, Han L, Sun J
abstract: Intervertebral disc degeneration (IVDD) has been a major contributor to chronic low back pain, yet effective disease-modifying therapies remain limited. Here, we identified a NOX4-associated ferro-aging program linking iron overload, oxidative stress, lipid peroxidation, and cellular senescence in degenerative NPCs. Clinical imaging, transcriptomic analyses, human disc specimens, iron-overloaded NPCs, and naturally aged rats consistently revealed ferro-aging-associated changes during IVDD. Mechanistically, gain- and loss-of-function, genetic rescue, and temporal analyses positioned NOX4 as an upstream oxidative regulator of ROS-dependent ACSL4 activation, lipid peroxidation, mitochondrial dysfunction, and NPC senescence. Natural-product screening identified amentoflavone (Amen) as a candidate NOX4-interacting compound that suppresses membrane-associated NADPH oxidase activity in a NOX4-dependent manner. Single-cell transcriptomic analyses showed that ferro-aging NPCs exhibited increased NKG2D ligand-related stress signals, reduced endocytic activity, and enhanced membrane-fusion features. Guided by these characteristics, we engineered SenoFAN, an Amen-loaded, iron-chelating phenolic nanozyme coated with NKG2D-engineered NPC membranes. SenoFAN integrates iron sequestration, nanozyme-mediated redox remodeling, Amen-mediated NOX4-dependent suppression of NADPH oxidase activity, and ferro-aging-cell-adapted delivery through NKG2D-ligand recognition and membrane fusion. In vitro, SenoFAN reduced labile iron and oxidative stress, restored mitochondrial and lipid homeostasis, and suppressed lipid peroxidation and senescence. In a rat puncture-induced IVDD model, SenoFAN showed preferential association with ferro-aging-associated NPCs, prolonged intradiscal retention, reduced iron deposition and senescence, preserved disc structure, and showed favorable biosafety. Collectively, our findings identify NOX4-associated ferro-aging as a therapeutically actionable pathological program in IVDD, while establishing an upstream regulatory role for NOX4 in the FAC-induced ferro-aging model.

title: Integrated UPLC-Q-Orbitrap-MS/MS, network pharmacology, and in vivo evaluation reveal bioactive constituents and mechanisms of Bushen Tongluo Decoction against idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis.
authors: Li K, Huang G, Ye Q, Cui H, Miao Q, Ren P
journal: Journal of pharmaceutical and biomedical analysis
abstract: The active constituents and mechanisms of Bushen Tongluo Decoction (BTD) in idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis (IPF) remain unclear. We profiled BTD constituents and serum compounds by ultra‑high‑performance liquid chromatography‑quadrupole‑Orbitrap high‑resolution tandem mass spectrometry (UPLC-Q-Orbitrap-MS/MS) and combined network pharmacology, in vivo evaluation, molecular docking, molecular dynamics (MD) simulation, and surface plasmon resonance (SPR) analysis to identify candidate bioactive compounds and associated mechanisms.We identified 614 constituents in BTD and 100 serum compounds, including 50 prototype compounds and 50 metabolites; 32 met Level 1 identification criteria. Network pharmacology identified 171 shared targets and prioritized transforming growth factor‑beta (TGF-β)- and mitogen‑activated protein kinase (MAPK)-related pathways. BTD reduced histopathological injury, collagen accumulation, and α‑smooth muscle actin (α‑SMA) and fibronectin 1 (FN1) expression, with stronger effects at the higher dose. Treatment was associated with changes in TGF-β1, Smad2/3, extracellular signal‑regulated kinase (ERK), and their phosphorylated forms. Ellagic acid showed the most favorable predicted binding energy at the latency-associated peptide (LAP)- growth factor (GF) interface of TGF-β1. MD analyses supported relative complex stability and yielded an estimated binding free energy of -59.43 ± 4.79 kJ/mol. SPR analysis detected binding between ellagic acid and TGF-β1, yielding a KD of 3.63 × 10⁻⁶ M. These findings indicate that BTD attenuated experimental pulmonary fibrosis and nominate ellagic acid as a candidate active constituent, and support the involvement of TGF-β1/Smads/ERK-related signaling in its effects on experimental pulmonary fibrosis.

title: Pharmacokinetic comparison of 18 constituents from Qingxin Zishen Prescription in normal and ovariectomized rats via a validated HPLC-MS/MS method.
authors: Xie K, Sui J, Hu Y, Li Y, Chen J, Sun H, Liu L, Zhu K
journal: Journal of pharmaceutical and biomedical analysis
abstract: Qingxin Zishen Prescription (QZP) is an empirical formula for treating menopausal syndrome, yet the pharmacokinetic behavior of its constituents under pathological conditions remains poorly understood. In the present work, we developed and validated a sensitive high-performance liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (HPLC-MS/MS) method to simultaneously quantify 18 representative bioactive constituents of QZP in rat plasma, and applied it to a comparative pharmacokinetic study in normal and ovariectomized (OVX) rats. Sample preparation involved protein precipitation with acetonitrile followed by concentration. Separation was achieved on an Agilent ZORBAX SB C18 column (4.6 ×100 mm, 1.8 μm), and detection was performed on a triple quadrupole mass spectrometer in both positive and negative modes. The method showed excellent linearity (r > 0.9965) with lower limits of quantification ranging from 0.015 to 25 ng/mL. The within-run and between-run precision (relative standard deviation, RSD) were within 8.58% and 10.37%, respectively, and the accuracy ranged from 85% to 115% at all quality control levels. Matrix effects ranged from 1.98% to 14.57% (RSD), and extraction recoveries ranged from 85.54% to 113.29%, both within acceptable limits. Stability under different storage conditions was also verified. The comparative pharmacokinetic study revealed that the t1/2 of rhynchophylline, corynoxeine, hirsuteine, magnoflorine, and catalpol were significantly prolonged in OVX rats, whereas that of demethyleneberberine was significantly shortened. In addition, hirsuteine showed significantly increased Cmax and AUC0-t, suggesting enhanced absorption in the pathological state. The results clarify the systemic exposure behavior of the main bioactive components of QZP and highlight marked pharmacokinetic differences between healthy and OVX rats. These findings indicate that estrogen deficiency significantly modulates the elimination and systemic exposure of multiple QZP constituents, suggesting that dose adjustment may be necessary when administering herbal medicines to menopausal patients.

Microfluidic integrated nucleic acid test (MINT) enabled by coupling FEN1-aided RPA with wax-purification and bead-carrier.
authors: Xu Z, Gao X, Huang J, Pang S, Wang S, Wang Y, Feng L, Ma Y
abstract: To guide timely antibiotic treatment, a tool for quick antimicrobial resistance gene detection is required. Here a Microfluidic Integrated Nucleic Acid Test platform (namely, MINT) was proposed for point-of-care molecular diagnostics. The platform integrates fast nucleic acid extraction based on hybrid wax-phase purification, and DNA amplification based on our newly developed FEN1-aided RPA (FARPA) into a microfluidic chip. The wax-phase stays solid at room temperature, while becomes liquid at >50 °C to allow the wash of inhibitors carried from extraction buffer, thus the chip keeps stable during storage and transportation. The movement of extracted DNA bound with magnetic beads were controlled by a magnet. The beaded DNA was quickly purified during the flow through the wax phase, and the amplification started once the beaded DNA reached to the well for FARPA. The signal from target-positive sample could be readily sensed by a conventional smartphone. The turnaround time is about 40 min from the sample to the result. The platform was validated by detecting the blaKPC-2 resistance gene of Klebsiella pneumoniae (K. pneumoniae) from urine samples with the reliable detection concentration of 500 CFU/mL, achieving 100% agreement for the 29 clinical urine samples (19 positive, 10 negative) with conventional qPCR. It is easy to adapt the MINT to any other pathogen only by designing the corresponding primers and probes for FARPA. It is promising to apply MINT for bed-site antimicrobial resistance screening just after operation.

title: Decoding bacterial identity and resistance through D-amino acid metabolic fingerprinting with a cascade colorimetric sensor array.
authors: Yang X, Yang D, Sun W, Song Y, Yang B, Huang P, Liu J, Gao X
abstract: The rapid rise of antimicrobial resistance (AMR) constitutes a global health crisis, demanding diagnostic tools capable of simultaneous bacterial identification and rapid antibiotic susceptibility testing (AST) in a single workflow. Herein, a colorimetric sensor array was developed to address this need by profiling bacterial metabolic fingerprints via a streamlined single-substrate, multi-wavelength strategy. The strategy is built upon the inherent bacteria-specific metabolism of D-amino acids (D-AAs), coupled with the enzymatic selectivity of D-amino acid oxidase (DAAO), which catalyzes the oxidation of D-AAs to generate H2O2. Differential bacterial consumption of D-Ala directly modulates the substrate available for the subsequent DAAO-coupled cascade reaction, producing varying amounts of H2O2. Consequently, H2O2 triggers the peroxidase (POD)-like activity of Prussian blue-coated gold nanoparticle (Au@PB NP) nanozyme to produce distinct multi-wavelength optical patterns from TMB oxidation. When coupled with linear discriminant analysis (LDA), this sensing platform enables clear discrimination of bacterial species based on their metabolic fingerprints. Moreover, by assessing the antibiotic-induced inhibition of this metabolic activity, the platform accurately determines bacterial susceptibility profiles, achieving 100% concordance with the standard disk diffusion method for both reference and clinical isolates, and successfully determining minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC) values for reference strains in full agreement with Clinical Laboratory Standards Institute (CLSI) breakpoint interpretation. This work establishes an integrated, rapid, and robust metabolic sensing platform for bacterial phenotyping and AST, offering a promising tool to combat AMR.

title: Sensitive detection of 4-hydroxy-2-nonenal-modified proteins in oxidative stress-related diseases.
authors: Méndez-Cuadro D, Kamali AN, Ruiz C, Pérez-Benavente S, Hernáez ML, Rodríguez-Cavallo E, Puyet A, Bautista JM
abstract: Protein modification by 4-hydroxy-2-nonenal (HNE) is associated with metabolic, neurodegenerative, and infectious diseases characterized by oxidative stress. Detecting low-abundance HNE-protein adducts in complex extracts requires antibodies with suitable reactivity and selectivity. We generated polyclonal antisera in rabbits using matched-species rabbit serum albumin modified in vitro with HNE (RSA-HNE), administered either intact or after tryptic digestion. The antisera displayed distinct recognition profiles across dot blot, ELISA, and Western blot assays using HNE-modified standards and membrane-protein extracts from uninfected and Plasmodium falciparum-infected human erythrocytes. Antiserum 1, raised against intact RSA-HNE, showed the stronger overall immunochemical response, whereas Antiserum 2, raised against tryptic RSA-HNE, displayed a different and more restricted peptide-recognition profile. In an immunoenrichment and LC-MS/MS workflow, Antiserum 1 recovered 14 candidate HNE-associated membrane proteins from erythrocytes infected with P. falciparum trophozoites. Site-specific evidence remained tentative for four peptides. These antisera are therefore proposed as research tools for studying protein lipoxidation, although biological replication and orthogonal validation of the candidate modification sites are required.

title: Proceedings of the 3rd edition of the International e-Health Forum 2024.
Beyond stroke: atrial fibrillation and the broader burden of thromboembolic events in the population-based EpiHealth study.
authors: Höiby P, Zarrouk M, Lind L, Basna R, Overton MC, Elmståhl S
abstract: OBJECTIVES: To investigate the distribution and risk of thromboembolic events (TEs) among adults with and without atrial fibrillation (AF), and to assess oral anticoagulant (OAC) use over time. DESIGN: This population-based longitudinal cohort study included EpiHealth participants recruited between April 2011 and December 2016 and followed through linkage to Swedish health data registers from baseline until the first TE, death, or December 31, 2016. RESULTS: At baseline, 873 of 22,616 participants (3.9%) had AF and 297 developed incident AF during follow-up. 484 participants experienced at least one TE during 70,587 person-years. Participants with AF had higher TE incidence (68 events, 5.9%; p < 0.001), predominantly arterial (73.5%), with 94% of arterial events involving the cerebral circulation. Approximately one quarter of TEs among participants with AF occurred outside the cerebral circulation and comprised both venous and non-cerebral arterial events. Although participants with incident AF represented less than one quarter of participants with AF, they accounted for 40% of TEs in the AF group. OAC use increased from 39.0% to 50.4%, with a shift from predominantly warfarin to direct oral anticoagulants. In time-dependent Cox regression adjusted for age, sex, and prior arterial thromboembolism, untreated AF was associated with increased thromboembolic risk compared with no AF (HR 2.53), whereas OAC use was associated with lower risk. CONCLUSIONS: AF was associated with substantially increased thromboembolic risk, predominantly arterial in nature. One in five TEs among participants with AF coincided with newly diagnosed AF, suggesting potential opportunities for earlier AF detection and timely initiation of anticoagulant treatment.

title: Circulatory arrest versus aortic cross-clamping in proximal thoracic aortic aneurysm repair.
authors: Braatz E, Stenman M, Al-Mousli J, Dalén M, Olsson C
abstract: INTRODUCTION: Aortic cross‑clamping and mild hypothermic circulatory arrest (MHCA) are commonly used strategies in proximal thoracic aortic aneurysm surgery. This study compared these approaches in elective procedures for patients with a distal ascending aortic diameter of 40-50 mm. The primary outcome was a composite of 30‑day mortality, stroke, or acute kidney injury, with secondary outcomes including long‑term survival and postoperative complications. MATERIAL AND METHODS: This single‑center observational cohort included patients treated between 2016 and 2024. Distal ascending aortic diameters were assessed on preoperative computed tomography, and clinical data were obtained from SWEDEHEART. Patients were assigned to aortic cross‑clamp (n = 261) or MHCA (n = 138). Propensity score matching was performed in a 1:1 ratio to balance baseline characteristics. RESULTS: The composite primary outcome occurred in 15 patients (3.8%) and was more common with MHCA than with cross‑clamp (6.5% vs 2.3%, p = 0.035). Two patients (0.5%), both in the MHCA group, died within 30 days. After matching, the odds ratio for the composite endpoint was 2.4 (95% CI, 0.66-11.5), indicating no significant difference. Long‑term survival was similar between groups (log‑rank p = 0.33). CONCLUSIONS: Both strategies were associated with low perioperative risk and comparable long‑term survival. These results support flexible operative planning, allowing the distal anastomotic technique to be chosen based on individual anatomy and surgical preference.

title: Biomimetic sequential targeted nanoplatform for synergistic thrombolysis in ischemic stroke.
authors: Wang J, Wang X, Liu S, Zheng Y, Wang C, Cheng J, Wang X
abstract: Conventional thrombolytic drugs for vascular blockage such as tissue plasminogen activator (tPA) are challenged by the low bioavailability, off-target side effects and limited penetration in thrombi, leading to delayed recanalization. Herein, we developed a sequential targeted nanoplatform for efficient thrombolysis based on the thrombolysis-neuroprotection integrated strategy. The mesoporous silica layer-modified upconversion nanoparticle (UCNP) was loaded with the nitric oxide (NO) donors (BNN6), further coating platelet membranes (PMs) on the surface of UCNP. tPA was conjugated onto PMs using the MMP9-responsive peptide as a linker to form a multifunctional drug carrier of UCNP/BNN6@PM-tPA. The proposed drug carrier maintained stability in the blood circulation to reduce bleeding risk (protection), facilitating it colonizing at the thrombus clots. MMP-9 triggered the release of tPA to realize rapid thrombolysis (attack), whereas continuous NO release from NIR-irradiated BNN6 acted to prevent vascular re-embolization (defense). In vitro and in vivo evaluation revealed that UCNP/BNN6@PM-tPA enables thrombus-homing accumulation, fluorescence imaging-guided thrombolysis, and NO mediated prevention of thrombosis recurrence, displaying favorable therapeutic outcomes with low bleeding risk. This study offers a facile, safe, and effective way towards the clinical treatment of thrombosis and ischemic stroke.

title: TMRKP: Trustworthy MRI-based radiology knowledge-aware prediction framework for stroke-associated pneumonia and hemorrhagic transformation.
authors: Zhao C, Yu Y, Xia T, Yuan M, Yang Y, Hu C
journal: Neural networks : the official journal of the International Neural Network Society
abstract: Prediction of stroke-associated pneumonia (SAP) and hemorrhagic transformation (HT) is critical for improving the prognosis of acute ischemic stroke patients. However, current brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)-based models narrowly focus on generic visual patterns, and frequently overlook the radiology-informed knowledge critical for predicting SAP and HT. To address this limitation, we propose a trustworthy MRI-based radiology knowledge-aware prediction (TMRKP) framework equipped with radiology knowledge-aware masked modeling (RKMM) and evidential multi-sequence fusion (EMF). Specifically, TMRKP first organizes four MRI sequences into a 2 × 2 super-sequence configuration, mimicking the diagnostic perspective of radiologists who simultaneously analyze multiple imaging modalities. Second, to introduce radiology knowledge into representation learning, we focus on white matter hyperintensities (WMH), a well-established biomarker of chronic small-vessel disease and long-term ischemic injury that is clinically relevant to SAP and HT. During pre-training, RKMM segments WMH masks from the MRI sequence to steer the model toward WMH regions, enabling it to learn meaningful representations of these clinically relevant pathological areas. Third, for SAP and HT prediction, EMF models the predictive uncertainty using evidence derived from both the super-sequence and the WMH-aware masked super-sequence, and fuses the resulting multi-sequence evidence based on Dempster-Shafer theory (DST). Extensive experiments on the collected Jiangdu dataset, together with independent external validation on the Zhongda dataset, demonstrate the superiority and generalizability of TMRKP over the state-of-the-art models.

title: SF2O-SKDCN: Selective kernel attention enabled deep learning framework for cardiovascular disease detection using photoplethysmography signals.
authors: Chavan PM, Joshi KR, Kamathe RS
abstract: Cardiovascular Disease (CVD) is a lethal disease that needs early intervention to prevent further harm and eventually safeguard patients' lives. Therefore, CVD detection is critical for effective disease management. Even though practical findings are made using traditional detection methods, they mostly struggle with overfitting risks, generalizability issues, and computational overhead challenges during the detection process. Therefore, the research proposes Sail Tuna Fish Foraging Optimized-Selective Kernel attention-enabled Deep Convolutional Neural Network (SF2O-SKDCN) that utilizes photoplethysmography (PPG) signals, which are extensively used in clinical applications as a screening tool, and the heart rate feature descriptor is introduced to extract the crucial feature from the segmented signal. Further, the Selective Kernel Shuffle (SKS) attention enables the model to focus only on the predominant CVD features, thereby enhancing the interpretability characteristics. In addition, actively tuning the model hyperparameters using the Sail Tuna Fish Foraging Optimization (SF2O) algorithm prevents local convergence and vanishing gradient issues. Experimenting with the MIMIC II dataset, the model yields better results by achieving 98.54% accuracy, 99.07% recall, 98.05% Positive predictive value, and 99.05% Negative predictive value for 90% training.

title: From laboratory quantification to rapid on-site testing: Screening of high-affinity monoclonal antibody pairs targeting the RSV F protein and analytical evaluation across multiple assay platforms.
authors: Peng S, Liu Q, Duan C, Liu J, Wang R, Huang Y, Long A, Deng Q
abstract: Monoclonal antibodies against respiratory syncytial virus (RSV) F protein are key reagents for antigen-based diagnosis, yet antibody pairs compatible with multiple assay formats remain limited. In this study, BALB/c mice were immunized with recombinant postfusion RSV F protein, yielding six hybridoma cell lines secreting anti-RSV F monoclonal antibodies. The antibodies were characterized by indirect ELISA, Western blotting, and surface plasmon resonance, and the optimal sandwich pair was selected by cross-pairing ELISA. The mAb-14/mAb-26 pair showed high affinity and the best pairing performance and was used to establish double-antibody sandwich ELISA (DAS-ELISA), magnetic microparticle-based chemiluminescent immunoassay, and Au@Pt nanoparticle-based lateral flow immunoassay (Au@Pt-LFIA). The limits of detection were 0.25, 0.04, and 0.78 ng/mL, respectively. Au@Pt-LFIA achieved an approximately fourfold lower visual detection limit than conventional colloidal gold immunochromatography without additional signal-amplification steps. None of the three methods showed detectable cross-reactivity with the seven tested heterologous respiratory pathogen antigens. In preliminary clinical sample testing, the positive percent agreements of DAS-ELISA, chemiluminescent immunoassay, and Au@Pt-LFIA were 90.0%, 93.3%, and 83.3%, respectively, and the negative percent agreements were 100.0% for all methods. These results support mAb-14/mAb-26 as a versatile antibody pair for RSV antigen detection across complementary laboratory and on-site assay platforms.

title: Guanidine-quaternary ammonium polymer-derived carbon dots differentially modulate bacterial respiration and osteoblast mitochondria to resolve infection and foster osteointegration.
authors: Bai X, Qin A, Wang Z, Kong G, Zhang M, Li H, Zhao R, Yu Y
abstract: Implant-associated infections (IAIs) represent one of the most challenging complications following orthopedic implantation. Current antibacterial strategies struggle to achieve complete pathogen eradication while maintaining sustained osteogenic activity at the implant-bone interface. Leveraging the spatial divergence in energy metabolism between prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells, we designed and synthesized guanidine-quaternary ammonium polymer-derived carbon dots (GQCDs) with confirmed structure. Under non-infected conditions, GQCDs enhance mitochondrial metabolism to promote bone regeneration. In infected microenvironments, GQCDs not only selectively target bacterial membranes and inhibit the respiratory chain to exert potent antibacterial effects, but also downregulate host inflammatory responses and restore mitochondrial function in osteoblasts, thereby creating a favorable microenvironment for bone repair. GQCDs can be stably integrated onto various clinical implant substrates via a coating process. GQCDs-coated implants possessed the dual antibacterial and osteogenic functionalities, which were validated using in vitro co-culture systems and in vivo implant infection models in rats and beagles, offering a promising strategy with encouraging translational prospects to address IAIs.

title: Gut microbiota and metabolic characteristics in PWHIV with metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD).
authors: Liu H, Xu T, Guo Y, Zhou X, Yan C, Zhu B, Xie Y
abstract: The global prevalence of Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) among persons with HIV (PWHIV) is estimated at 34%. This study examined the influence of gut microbial and metabolic alterations in PWHIV with MASLD. We conducted 16S rRNA sequencing on 60 fecal samples (24 from HIV group and 36 from HIV-MASLD group) to assess microbial composition, and employed LC/MS-based metabolomics on both fecal and plasma samples to identify variations in metabolites. An exploratory analysis was performed to compare plasma cytokines and oxidative stress markers between the two groups. Sequencing in the HIV-MASLD group showed lower Faecalibacterium and Anaerobutyricum, and higher Klebsiella, Escherichia, and Enterococcus. Metabolomic analysis revealed a reduction in anti-inflammatory metabolites (Dodecanedioic acid, 5-Phenylvaleric acid, Kynurenic acid) and antioxidant metabolites, coupled with an increase in the pro-inflammatory metabolite Gamma-Glutamyl-L-Putrescine in the HIV-MASLD group. And plasma analysis indicated a decline in 20-carboxy arachidonic acid. Additionally, Faecalibacterium and Anaerobutyricum correlated positively with anti-inflammatory metabolites, while Klebsiella, Enterobacter, and Citrobacter correlated negatively. Furthermore, Faecalibacterium and Anaerobutyricum also showed a moderate negative correlation with MDA levels. A random forest model using plasma metabolites showed the optimal discriminative ability for HIV-MASLD (AUC = 0.819 ± 0.0059). Differences in gut microbiota and metabolites in PWHIV may affect MASLD progression by influencing inflammation and oxidative stress. Modulating gut microbiota, such as adding Faecalibacterium and Anaerobutyricum, could be a treatment strategy for HIV-MASLD. Plasma metabolites have potential as noninvasive markers.

title: Inflammation-anchored injectable hydrogel integrating pathological nitric oxide scavenging and on-demand drug release for localized inflammatory bowel disease therapy.
authors: Eom S, Lee S, Boo Y, Kim J, Kim WJ
abstract: Inflammatory bowel disease (IBD), encompassing chronic relapsing gastrointestinal disorders, remains a profound clinical challenge because conventional therapeutics are often impeded by systemic off-target toxicities and suboptimal retention at inflamed mucosal sites. Herein, an inflammation-activated and retentive injectable hydrogel is presented, which leverages pathological nitric oxide (NO) overproduction as both a therapeutic target and an autonomous release trigger. An NO-responsive and NO-scavenging polymer (NRSP) incorporating an NO-cleavable o-phenylenediamine (o-PD) motif is formulated into cationic, dexamethasone-encapsulating micelles and electrostatically assembled with anionic hyaluronic acid (HA) to form a shear-thinning hydrogel that facilitates minimally invasive rectal administration and ensures prolonged, localized retention at the inflamed mucosal interface. Upon exposure to the NO-rich inflammatory microenvironment, structural disruption of NO-responsive and NO-scavenging micelles (NRSM) compromises the electrostatic integrity of the HA-micelle network, thereby reducing the storage modulus and accelerating cargo release. In vitro evaluations using lipopolysaccharide-stimulated macrophages demonstrate that NRSM hydrogels effectively reduce intracellular and extracellular NO levels and attenuate pro-inflammatory cytokine secretion. Furthermore, the HA matrix mediates disease-adaptive localization through CD44 receptor recognition and preferential electrostatic adhesion to positively charged inflammatory interfaces, resulting in enhanced colonic retention in DSS-induced colitis models ex vivo. Following rectal administration in DSS-induced mice, NRSM-based hydrogels significantly alleviate disease severity, reduce colonic NO and inflammatory cytokine levels, and rescue mucosal architecture and mucin-associated features. Notably, dexamethasone-loaded NRSM hydrogel exerted the most potent synergistic therapeutic benefit. Overall, this disease-responsive hydrogel platform establishes an effective localized intervention for IBD, merging intrinsic pathological NO scavenging with controlled drug delivery.

title: Hematopoietic cell transplantation using treosulfan-based conditioning for IL-10 receptor deficiency.
authors: Lakkaraja M, Schmitt EG, Sood AK, Chen K, Modi AJ, Verbsky JW, Torgerson T, Wahbeh G
abstract: IL-10 receptor deficiency is a life-threatening inborn error of immunity associated with early-onset inflammatory bowel disease. Hematopoietic cell transplantation (HCT) using treosulfan-based conditioning resulted in excellent survival with full donor engraftment. Importantly, anakinra effectively served as a bridge to HCT.

title: Baseline monocyte SGLT2 mRNA expression and changes in the fibrosis-4 index after luseogliflozin treatment in participants with type 2 diabetes and MASLD.
authors: Okuma H
abstract: BACKGROUND: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is common in type 2 diabetes. We investigated the association between monocyte mRNA expression of sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 (SGLT2), the molecular target of luseogliflozin, and changes in the fibrosis-4 (FIB-4) index during treatment with this agent. METHODS: This single-center retrospective observational study used prospectively collected peripheral blood monocyte samples from 82 participants with type 2 diabetes and MASLD who had received luseogliflozin for at least 6 months. Baseline monocyte SGLT2 mRNA expression was measured using quantitative real-time polymerase chain reaction. Clinical and laboratory parameters, including FIB-4 index, were evaluated at baseline and 6 months after luseogliflozin initiation. Changes were calculated as the 6-month value minus the baseline value; therefore, negative values indicated reductions. RESULTS: After 6 months, waist circumference, hemoglobin A1c, liver enzyme levels, high-sensitivity C-reactive protein, and the FIB-4 index decreased significantly. Baseline monocyte SGLT2 mRNA expression was negatively correlated with the change in the FIB-4 index, indicating that higher baseline expression was associated with a greater reduction. In multiple regression analyses, natural-log-transformed baseline monocyte SGLT2 mRNA expression remained associated with the change in the FIB-4 index after adjustment for baseline clinical variables. CONCLUSIONS: Higher baseline monocyte SGLT2 mRNA expression was associated with a greater reduction in the FIB-4 index after luseogliflozin treatment. This finding should be interpreted as an exploratory association between a cell-specific transcriptomic feature and changes in a fibrosis-related index, rather than as evidence of functional SGLT2 signaling in monocytes or histological fibrosis regression. SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION: The online version contains supplementary material available at https://doi.org/10.1007/s13340-026-00941-2.
